analysis: The PR modifies only docs/reference/configuration.md. No executable code, so no direct security regression. I examined head_text lines 314-675 (units 10 and 11): schedule windows, model cache location, daemon/path env vars, engine/scheduler tuning, MiMo/Qwen4/Diffusion/Bonsai flags, memory/media budgets, hash-verification I/O, prompt prep, and SSD prefix cache config. These excerpts appear unchanged context. The patch excerpt (truncated) shows the real change is in the cluster runtime facts section (head ~923-1076, outside the supplied units): release registration now carries a `cluster_runtime` block in the POST /v1/releases payload, and a coordinator accepting it derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it. This is a potentially material trust-flow change (A-005 release API key, A-011 binary hash registry, A-017 build qualifications, TB-011), but the code is not in the supplied units and is documentation-only here, so no finding is asserted. Cache-related docs in the supplied lines (cache.directory, cache.daily_write_gb, model_cache_directory) are consistent with the T-041 operator-selected storage posture; no TTL/encryption weakening is described. The documented DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE record binds device/inode/size/mtime/ctime and is consistent with existing T-012/T-027 posture. Remaining integration question: whether the cluster_runtime release-registration path (coordinator derivation of approvals/grants) is backed by independent qualification rather than release-key-only trust, and whether the threat model should record that as a new trust dependency. That text lies in head lines 923-995 and was not supplied here.
